quotes.text: There isn't anything existing so root can be required from the start
quotes.where: answer on what happens to a repo under no root

fields.summary: The owner planned milestone 28, in which Rhiza manages and builds several projects on one machine from one root directory. Picked options: one root daemon per machine drives every project under one usage governor and one machine-wide run cap, and serves one web UI. Projects are registered explicitly under the root (rhiza project add, by path or git URL). Run slots are shared round-robin across projects, in each project's roadmap order, with an optional per-project max. Machine-wide settings live in the root config and per-project settings stay in each repo's git config. The web UI gets an all-projects home and a merged inbox, plus per-project pages through a switcher. The CLI and the Rex TUI apps go multi-project in this milestone. Worktrees stay as <root>/<project>.<slug> siblings. A registered project with no .rhiza/ is listed but not built. Each project keeps its own Rex session. All six change sets (root and registry, root daemon, cross-project CLI, web UI, TUI apps, VM migration) are planned now. In a typed answer, the owner ruled that a root is required from the start, with no per-repo daemon mode kept.
fields.title: Milestone 28 interview: many projects from one root
